ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: In the figure, there are three congruent squares placed horizontally side by side, the bottom side points are labeled from left to right as A, B, C, D, and the top side points are labeled from left to right as H, G, F, E. Segment AE connects from the lower-left corner A to the upper-right corner E, segment CH connects from point C to the upper-left corner H, and the two lines intersect at P. What is required is the angle ∠CPE at P formed by rays PC and PE. Then reason: Let the side length of each square be 1. According to the three squares in the figure being horizontally adjacent, take coordinates A=(0,0), B=(1,0), C=(2,0), D=(3,0), H=(0,1), G=(1,1), F=(2,1), E=(3,1). The slope of line AE is (1-0)/(3-0)=1/3, so ray PE is inclined upward relative to the horizontal line by arctan(1/3). The slope of line CH is (1-0)/(0-2)=-1/2, so ray PC is inclined downward relative to the horizontal line by arctan(1/2). Therefore ∠CPE = arctan(1/3)+arctan(1/2). Using the tangent addition formula: tan(∠CPE)=((1/3)+(1/2))/(1-(1/3)(1/2))=(5/6)/(5/6)=1. Therefore ∠CPE=45°.

method.method_draft: Use coordinates and slopes. From the image, read that the three congruent squares are placed in a horizontal row, with bottom vertices A, B, C, D and top vertices H, G, F, E. Assign square side length 1, so A=(0,0), B=(1,0), C=(2,0), D=(3,0), H=(0,1), G=(1,1), F=(2,1), E=(3,1). The line AE has slope 1/3, so ray PE is inclined at arctan(1/3) above the horizontal. The line CH has slope (1-0)/(0-2)=-1/2, so ray PC is inclined at arctan(1/2) below the horizontal. Therefore angle CPE is arctan(1/3)+arctan(1/2). Use the tangent addition formula: tan(angle)=(1/3+1/2)/(1-(1/3)(1/2))=(5/6)/(5/6)=1, so the angle is 45 degrees.
